title: Smooth Cold Brew Coffee from Concentrate
summary: Coarse coffee steeps in cold water for 12-24 hours, is strained through a paper filter, then diluted 1:1 with cold water over ice.
equipment: large jar or cafetière (at least 1 litre)
bottle or jar with a lid, for storing

ingredients.note: as coarse as for a cafetière

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Put the coffee in the jar, pour in the 750 ml water and stir until all the grounds are wet. Wait 10 minutes for a crust to form, then stir again so nothing stays dry.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Cover and leave at room temperature for 12-24 hours; 12 hours gives a mellow brew, 24 a stronger one.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Line the sieve with the paper filter and set it over a jug. Pour the coffee through slowly, pressing the plunger first if using a cafetière, and let it drip. Don't squeeze the filter, or the brew turns cloudy and bitter. You should have about 550 ml concentrate.

steps.title: Dilute and serve
steps.text: Fill 4 glasses with ice and add equal parts concentrate and cold water, about 135 ml of each per glass. Top with milk if you like.

tips: Grind coarsely: fine grounds over-extract and clog the filter.
Use filtered water if your tap water tastes of chlorine.
Strain twice through fresh filters for the clearest coffee.
Freeze some diluted cold brew as ice cubes to keep the glass strong.
storage: Undiluted concentrate keeps in a lidded bottle in the fridge for up to 1 week. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
